$comment: Written by `nen scaffold init`. This file is POLICY -- what the delivery loop's parameters are. What nen EXECUTES lives in nen/contract.json. Every key here is optional and carries the default nen applies when it is absent; delete anything you do not want to state. `nen schema check` validates it.

deploy.$comment: defaultTarget names the project.targets key a caller's own tooling sends to when told no target; it must be declared "nonProduction": true. null means ask. nen shu deploy never reads it and still requires --target.

notifications.$comment: turn decides how loud an ORDINARY (no-gate) turn is: 'rung1' rings only the first rung 'rungs' lists, 'all' rings every rung 'rungs' lists on every turn -- a gate always rings everything 'rungs' lists regardless.

commits.$comment: Hatsu-Agent (a local-plane agent, working on a human's own credentials) and Akatsuki-Agent (an autonomous CI-plane agent) are the two conventional provenance-trailer keys this project's family uses -- never an AI-authorship claim. nen ships neither as a default: this list stays empty until a repository states which of the two (or both) it admits, e.g. ["Hatsu-Agent", "Akatsuki-Agent"]. `nen scaffold init`'s own --agent-trailer defaults to Akatsuki-Agent and writes its resolved key here for you. runTrailer is a SEPARATE, OPTIONAL key, e.g. "Akatsuki-Run" -- absent (null) by default, and never itself an attribution trailer: it names which RUN produced a commit, not who or what did, so it never belongs in the list above. Set it (--run-trailer, then re-run 'nen scaffold init' to regenerate the hook) only if this repository also wants a run identifier required on every automated commit.

models.$comment: An open map at both levels: a surface is whatever you call it, a tier likewise. nen validates that every leaf is a string and reads nothing else -- these aliases are for whoever asks the question, not for nen.
models.rule: latest alias only, never a version; subagents never on the frontier tier

cursor.note: surface-native aliases only; provider models on this surface are reserved for its own review bot

review.$comment: hanten routes a diff by these scopes; code claims every path (the default reviewer), ui the rendered surface, security the workflows and build scripts, performance the bundle-bearing sources. Budgets are per effort.

pr.$sections: available sections: delivery — Always-first ledger-rendered delivery metadata; outside the seven-reader cap. | changes — Before/After for a named consumer; Case for/Case against; what would flip the decision. | why — Source/What it showed/Why it matters now, followed by the authoring nature. | how — Mermaid structure diagram and Item/Kind/Change legend; flow diagram only when behavior flow changed; one rejected alternative. | improves — All eleven aspects, marked ⬆ improves / ➖ unchanged / ⬇ regresses; justify only movement. | verify — Product: numbered steps. Library: Consumer scenario/Call or import/Expected, plus published artifact command. Process: Behavior changed/Lane or verb run/Refuses on/Passes on. Every kind adds one Criterion/Coverage/Evidence row per AC id of each closing issue (HR-11; judged by nen pr converge). content: an empty heading fails body-check through the derived verify-content requirement. | evidence — UZF-26 state/variant evidence table; only where project.evidence.globs is declared. | compat — Symbol/Before/After/Consumer action; semver verdict. | across — What another repository does differently after this merge; recorded rulings. | release-unit — Artifact/Size/Provenance; CON-22 fan-out. | rollout — Target/Flag/Rollback step. | economics — Leorio summary, then the full report in details; no new level-2 headings inside it. | spec — One row per F<nnn>-SC-### the closing spec-derived issue carries, satisfied with a test id or deferred with a reason and a follow-up (docs/config/spec-repo.md, The PR Spec section). Admitted by the run fact spec; rows is nen's spec-rows requirement quoted whole (zheref/nen#493, src/spec/coverage.ts), and nen spec coverage's delivery form proves every criterion is accounted for. | decisions — Every pre-answered row and every default the run took for the maintainer; mandatory on every PR whose run took one, idle (HR-334) or attended (HA#474 AC-1), whatever the kind or family. Any positive source includes it: --decisions, --idle, or --decisions-from a nen.run manifest with a non-empty idleAnswers. A manifest proves only launch pre-answers: a null or empty idleAnswers adds nothing beside --decisions or --idle (the flag wins) and refuses alone; a malformed manifest refuses whatever else is passed. A default taken mid-run or attended is --decisions. | hanten — Exact adopted-gate heading and settled Hanten findings. Each deferred row cites a tracked issue. | prose — HA#503, HR-369: the four PRS rows (criteria, measurable, scope, markers) Chrollo answers on a canon-prose PR, each with a yes or no verdict and the line he read (line N or path:N), never the author. Admitted by the run fact canon-prose (--canon-prose, or --scopes-from a nen review scopes document in which Chrollo's scope claims a changed .md; the architecture globs in nen/workflow.json are canon prose's one definition); rows requires exactly one answered row per letter under the heading. A no is also a Hanten finding with rule PRS-<letter>, medium and pushable. docs/PR-SECTIONS.md section The prose checklist. | checklist — Compact evidence-backed completion conditions, including the checked Hanten-settled evidence line. | issues — Canonical issue URL/scope/merging verdict table and closing lines; Development guard applies. | attribution — Final heading; exact participant ledger from docs/AGENT-ATTRIBUTION.md.
